rows.description: The person tries a course, a side project or a conversation with someone doing what they admire. Cheap tests of a new direction give real feedback without burning bridges.
graph_context: previous stage: Sorting regret from values
next stage: Own timeline, own pace
related mind states: admiration

rows.description: Comfort comes from accepting that lives unfold unevenly and that many paths open late. The person plans in years, not weeks, and measures progress against their own values.
graph_context: previous stage: Small experiments

rows.description: A student or young worker arrives in a new city for study or a job, finding everything fresh and exciting. Novelty gives energy, and homesickness is pushed aside by the rush of activity.
graph_context: next stage: Logistics and small frustrations
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: excitement, nostalgia

rows.description: Finding a flat, food, language and paperwork wear the person down. Small irritations pile up, and the person compares everything unfavourably with home.
graph_context: previous stage: Excitement and honeymoon
next stage: Homesickness and culture shock
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: anger

rows.description: Weeks in, the person misses family, familiar food and being known, and feels like an outsider. Crying at night or a wish to return does not mean the move was wrong.
graph_context: previous stage: Logistics and small frustrations
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: sadness, surprise, nostalgia

rows.description: Parents at home feel the absence too, and worry when the child sounds low. Regular, warm calls without guilt-tripping or demands to return let the young person keep a base and still grow.
graph_context: previous stage: Logistics and small frustrations
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: anxiety, guilt, surprise, nostalgia

rows.subtype: Stage 4: Loneliness and testing the new place [Actor]
rows.description: Colleagues are friendly but distant, and weekends feel empty. The person tries clubs, neighbours or people from their region and finds that making friends takes months, not weeks.
graph_context: next stage: The low point
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: loneliness

rows.description: A bad week such as illness or a work setback in an unfamiliar place feels much worse without a support net. Doubt about the move peaks, and reaching out to someone can turn the stretch.
graph_context: previous stage: Loneliness and testing the new place
next stage: Building routines and roots
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: doubt

rows.description: The person finds a regular café, gym or community, learns local ways and keeps rituals from home. Familiar routines create steadiness while new ties form.
graph_context: previous stage: The low point
next stage: Two homes, one self
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: After a year or so, the place feels familiar and home is no longer only one location. The person keeps ties to both, feels gratitude for what each gave and can help a newcomer through the same path.
graph_context: previous stage: Building routines and roots
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: gratitude
